A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, central methods, theoretical results, and original ImageNet experiment. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ViT recalibration results on ImageNet in Table 1 and Figure 1, plus kernel-sensitivity experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds experiments with other ImageNet models, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and alternative calibration visualizations.

M1.justification: MRR retains the same confidence replacement and redistribution of remaining probability mass. Calibration-sharpness diagrams retain the same kernel regression estimates and density-weighted bands. The expanded explanations and stronger theoretical justification do not change these procedures.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only ImageNet-1K-Val. v2 Appendix F adds CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 classification evaluations while retaining ImageNet, substantially broadening the represented datasets and class counts.

E2.justification: v2 adds direct comparisons against conventional reliability diagrams in Figure 2 and SmoothECE visualizations in Appendix G/Figure 8. v1 discusses these approaches and reports SmoothECE as a metric but does not perform these visualization comparisons. The recalibration comparator set remains baseline, TS, HB, IR, and MRR.

E3.justification: The original ImageNet split, metrics, and binning settings remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B3, and ConvNeXt-Tiny configurations on ImageNet, ResNet-32 with 20% calibration splits on CIFAR, 15-bin reliability-diagram comparisons, and SmoothECE visualizations using 5,000 subsampled test examples. These substantially expand the evaluation settings without establishing reruns of the original experiment.

E4.justification: v2 tests whether the MRR phenomenon depends on model backbone through Appendix F and adds a confidence-region case study comparing HB and IR using alternative visualizations in Section 5.2 and Appendix G. The original Gaussian-bandwidth and Epanechnikov-kernel sensitivity analyses remain unchanged, moving from Appendix B to Appendix H.

E5.justification: Figure 8 newly reports uncertainty annotations for SmoothECE, such as 0.085 ± 0.008 for the baseline; v1 reports only SmoothECE point estimates. Their statistical construction is not specified. The existing practice of reporting means and standard deviations from ten 5,000-example subsamples is retained, with no stated increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Table 1 and all original calibration-sharpness plots retain their results. v2 adds Tables 2–6 and corresponding plots for five additional model/dataset settings. For example, CIFAR-100 Table 6 reports MRR versus TS ECE of 0.20 versus 1.71, but Brier scores of 50.63 versus 40.98, using the tables' factor-of-100 scaling. These are new evaluations, not improvements over v1 under the original setting.

T1.justification: v2 strengthens v1 Lemma 4.5's averaged inequality into the conditional, almost-sure bound in Lemma 4.6 and supplies an explicit band-nonnegativity proof in Proposition 4.8. Proposition 4.4 newly proves that only squared L2 ECE among the specified Lq errors is induced by a Bregman divergence. Proof signs and the consistency theorem's expected-error target are also corrected; the general data-processing corollary becomes an explicit KL/logistic-loss result.

C1.justification: v1 presents deriving the decomposition as a central contribution and suggests it has not previously been used. v2 reframes this as applying existing decomposition results, emphasizing the full-versus-confidence calibration bound and the visualization contribution instead. This substantively narrows the novelty claim while retaining the central recommendation to report calibration and generalization together.

C2.justification: v2 adds detailed interpretations of confidence concentration, HB/IR sharpness trade-offs, and the relationship to grouping loss in Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendix E. It removes v1's explicit limitations concerning scoring-rule selection and its warning that multiclass bands combine sharpness with the difference between full and confidence calibration errors.

D1.justification: v2 adds checkpoint identifiers, the CIFAR pretrained-model source, explicit PyTorch usage, and practical bandwidth-selection guidance. It retains the principal kernel and hardware details, largely relocating them to Appendix D. Code is described as available through supplementary material and sharpcal, but v1's explicit installation command and project repository URL are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises attribution of the decomposition, acknowledging more general prior results including Bröcker (2009) and Gruber and Buettner (2024). It adds Perez-Lebel et al. (2023) as the closest related work and devotes Appendix E to distinguishing grouping-loss estimation from its approach. Additional visualization and mathematical references further expand the positioning.

P1.justification: The theoretical narrative and diagram explanation are extensively rewritten. Diagram theory moves into Section 4.2, experiments receive a separate Section 5, proofs and implementation details are reorganized into Appendices A–D, and the original kernel analysis moves to Appendix H. The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion are revised, with a contents page and reproducibility statement added.

P2.justification: v2 adds five result tables, new model/dataset plots, SmoothECE plots, and Figure 2's aligned-axis comparison with reliability diagrams. Original Figure 1 is retained, and original Figures 2–7 become Figures 9–14 without changes to their plotted content. Conference formatting also changes typography, margins, headers, and figure placement.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens both the justification and validation of its visualization. The conditional bound and explicit nonnegativity proof better support confidence-specific bands, while broader model/dataset experiments address v1's reliance on a single ViT/ImageNet example. Direct visualization comparisons make the claimed diagnostic benefits easier to assess, and revised attribution corrects the novelty positioning. These gains outweigh the removal of explicit multiclass-band and scoring-rule caveats and some code-access details.
